headline: Graph, bias-correction, and filtering methods refine genomic and metagenomic inference
label: Genomic Analysis Tools
summary: Multi-sample graphs, GC-bias correction, and host-read filtering address confounding in metagenomic and WGS analyses before inference.
synthesis: The dominant thread is preprocessing and correction of genomic data before downstream inference. Copangraph builds multi-sample sequence graphs from hybrid coassembly and homology-based graphs for comparative metagenomic variation analysis, while GuaCAMOLE estimates and removes GC-content bias from single-sample species abundances, validated on 3435 colorectal cancer gut samples. A multi-step host-read filtering pipeline removes over 99.9% of human reads from rectal cancer WGS data, improving Fusobacterium detection. GrafGen applies genetic-distance clustering to Helicobacter pylori ancestry for GWAS stratification. Rider and COATswga address adjacent problems, RNA virus RdRp discovery and selective whole genome amplification primer design, without sharing this framing. What is new is the explicit graph formulation applied to multi-sample comparative data.
